audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields state Feast 'ignores the bonus armor/MR his passive grants'. Dauntless Instinct grants no resistances at all — Riot's text says his abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next attack. Separately, no field anywhere names Path Maker, Ntofo Strikes or Footwork, and the biggest interaction in the kit is missing: Path Maker's dash deals true damage.
audit.why: Attributing resistances to the passive teaches the player the wrong reason Feast works. The correct reason is simpler and always true: Feast is true damage at 175 range, so his resistances never mattered, and All Out explicitly trades defenses for damage when he commits. Path Maker dealing true damage is the reverse case — it means stacking armour reads his charge-dash trade wrong, which is exactly the mistake a Cho'Gath building Plated Steelcaps will make. Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s flat and at two stacks fires a shockwave that pulls, so it is a pull, not the 'wall' or 'knockup' the page calls it.
audit.corrected: Say Feast is true damage and All Out lowers his own defenses; name Path Maker's true-damage dash and Ntofo Strikes' two-stack pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and First item are scored Skill and K'Sante in both layers. The packet chart gives both to Cho'Gath, and the prose says so: 'Level 6 is my window', 'First item is still mine'.
audit.why: 48.82% over 381 games is a near-even lane whose shape is: K'Sante owns levels 2-3, Cho'Gath owns 6 through first item, K'Sante takes it back at two items. The chart currently gives K'Sante four rows and Cho'Gath none, which no paragraph on the page supports.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and First item flip to Cho'Gath, ratings 6/10 each. Rows 0-3 and row 6 already match the prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown number appears in either layer. 'Trade around All Out's cooldown' and 'punish him the moment that charge is on cooldown' are both untimed.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80 seconds and 250 range. Path Maker is 14s at rank 1 — that is the number the whole early game turns on, because the advice is literally 'trade after the charge'. Footwork is 10s at rank 1 and gives him a shield, which the page never mentions. Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s flat, so it is never a window.
audit.corrected: Put 120s (All Out), 14s (Path Maker) and 3.5s (Ntofo Strikes) into cooldowns, loading and the prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind' without naming the heal.
audit.why: All Out is the heal: Riot's text says K'Sante gains increased healing while transformed. That is a 120-second window at rank 1, so Grievous Wounds needs to already be on the board before he ults, not bought after the first bad duel.
audit.corrected: Name Bramble Vest and All Out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Voice: the entire content layer for this matchup is written in the first person ('belongs to him, not me', 'I'm slow and short-ranged', 'stabilize me'). Every other Cho'Gath matchup addresses the reader as 'you'. Two Common Mistakes headings also name the wrong ability — 'Get walled by his Q' (the wall is All Out) and 'Dodge his Q knockups' (Ntofo Strikes pulls, it does not knock up).
audit.why: A single page slipping into first person reads as a different writer, and mis-titled mistakes send the player watching the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrite early, mid, late and the affected whys in second person; retitle the two mistakes to All Out and the Ntofo pull.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to him, not me — I'm slow and short-ranged with no sustain edge yet, and his W charge into a wall stuns me while the same charge cuts the damage he takes, so he can step on and trade before Carnivore and Vorpal Spikes come online. Don't throw a lazy Rupture into his W charge — it just gets soaked; hold it and only commit Q-W once that charge is spent. Soak with the tip of my Q, eat a little chip, and remember his early is real but it doesn't snowball if I never eat the wall-stun.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to him. Path Maker charges up taking reduced damage, then dashes to knock you back and stun you — and that dash is true damage, so armour reads the trade wrong. Don't throw a lazy Rupture into the charge; it gets soaked. Hold Q until the charge is spent, then commit Q-W, because Path Maker is 14s at rank 1 and those fourteen seconds are your whole window. Farm at Rupture's 950 edge, keep Carnivore topping you up, and never give him a wall to pin you on.

edits.before: By 4-5 my Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes waveclear stabilize me and the lane levels out. Level 6 is my window — Feast is point-blank true damage that ignores the bonus armor and MR his passive piles on, so it deters his All Out all-in and finally gives me a kill threat his W reduction can't sponge. Bait the charge first: fake a Q or auto, and once his W is down, Rupture-knockup into Feral Scream to silence the recast, then auto with spikes. Punish him hardest the moment that damage-reduction charge is on cooldown.
edits.after: By 4-5 Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes waveclear stabilize you and the lane levels out. Level 6 is your window — Feast is point-blank true damage at 175 range, so no resistance he owns touches it, and All Out trades away his defenses the moment he commits. Bait Path Maker first: fake a Q or an auto, and once the charge is spent, Rupture-knockup into Feral Scream to silence the follow-up, then auto with spikes. Punish him hardest in the 14 seconds that charge is down.

edits.before: First item is still mine — Heartsteel/Sunfire plus Feast stacks make me a sticky monster who owns the extended trade his W can only blunt for one charge. But once he hits 2+ items the lane flips: All Out strips his own bonus resists for raw damage, knocks me back through a wall to isolate me, and his fighter form out-duels me one-on-one even through my stacked HP. Don't take the isolated fight late — group, peel with Rupture and the silence, and let Feast clean up in the teamfight instead of dueling his All Out solo.
edits.after: First item is still yours — Heartsteel/Sunfire plus Feast stacks make you the sticky monster who owns the extended trade one Path Maker charge can only blunt. But at 2+ items the lane flips: All Out is 120s at rank 1, knocks you back through a wall to isolate you, and heals him the whole time he duels, so Grievous Wounds has to already be built before he ults. Don't take that fight alone — group, peel with Rupture and the silence, and let Feast clean up the teamfight.
